derived.label: Units against the forecast at the spend that happened, year to date
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes a variance per month, not a year-to-date sum of them. This is that sum, over the months both figures cover, computed from the two figures it names.

derived.label: Units against what was expected before the year began, year to date
derived.why_not_published: This stands where a variance against the brand plan would go. The brand has no plan document, so there is nothing to measure against one; forecast.expected.year_start.units.ytd is what the model expected before the year began, and the difference is computed here rather than published as a figure of its own.

derived.label: Units against the forecast at the spend that happened, 2026-02
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes each month's variance against the forecast as it was made. Against the forecast at the spend that happened it publishes the two figures and not their difference, which is computed here from them.

derived.label: The current model's projection for 2026-02 against the same month a year earlier, units
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes the projection and the same month a year earlier, and not the one as a percentage of the other. It is computed here from the two figures it names.

derived.label: Projected units, 2026-03 to 2026-12
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes a projection per month, not their sum. This is the sum over the months it names, each at the spend its own figure stands on.

derived.label: Units for 2026-01 to 2026-12, actual to date plus projected
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes the year to date and each month's projection, not the two added together. This is that sum: what has closed, plus what the current model projects for the rest of the window.

derived.label: Change in units per 1 USD of ad spend when 2026-02 was added
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes the model and the refit that stops one month short of it, and not the difference between them. It is computed here from the two figures it names.

derived.label: Change in the units trend per month when 2026-02 was added
derived.why_not_published: The forecast document publishes the model and the refit that stops one month short of it, and not the difference between them. It is computed here from the two figures it names.

forecast_units_uncorrected.text: 2 of the 32 months this units model trains on have corrected sales and uncorrected units. The revenue forecast stands on those corrections; the units forecast still stands on the unit counts the source reports for the same months, so the two do not describe the same history.

forecast_units_no_plan.text: This brand has no approved plan in the forecast document, so no figure here is measured against one. The year-start series stands in: the forecast made at the end of 2025-12, which is what the model expected before the year began, not what anybody committed to.

forecast_units_long_horizon.text: The year-start figure is a twelve-month-horizon forecast. Across our whole book no training depth beat last year's same month at seven to twelve months out, so treat it as a planning baseline rather than a forecast.

forecast_units_projection_in_sample.text: A closed month's projection is the current model at the spend that happened, and the current model was fitted on that month among the others. It is the figure the forecasting app's Table shows as Projected Units. It is not a forecast made in advance: that figure is beside it, and it is the one a forecasting error is read from.

forecast_units_month_spend_estimated_at_.text: The forecast for 2026-02 was made at the end of 2026-01, at the ad spend the app estimated then. The forecast at the spend that actually happened is beside it.

forecast_units_spend_estimated.text: 1 month below (2026-06) stands on ad spend the app estimated, not on a budget anybody set. A projection moves with the spend it is given.

forecast_units_month_without_actuals.text: 6 months below (2026-03, 2026-04, 2026-05, 2026-06, 2026-07, 2026-08) have closed with no final figure in the forecast document. The value is the current model at the month's spend, not a forecast made in advance and not an actual.

forecast_units_model_drift_is_a_refit.text: The earlier figure is today's history refitted without 2026-02, corrections included. It says how the model moved when the month was added. It is not a record of what the app showed a month ago, which may have stood on different corrections.

forecast_units_overlay_source_moved.text: 1 correction in the forecasting app sits on a source figure that has moved since the correction was entered. The corrected figure stands; nothing was changed automatically.

claims.text: Units year to date are 28,493 against 28,737 projected by the current model at the spend that happened, a difference of -0.9%.

Units year to date are 28,493 against 28,917 forecast at the spend that actually happened, a difference of -1.5% against a measured error of 6.7% (this scope, replayed over 21 closed months) one to three months out.
Units for 2026-02 were 14,378 against 15,036 projected by the current model at the spend that happened, a difference of -4.4%. That projection is 13.6% above the same month a year earlier.

Before the month closed, it stood against 15,164 forecast at the spend that actually happened, a difference of -5.2% against a measured error of 6.7% (this scope, replayed over 21 closed months) one to three months out. The forecast made at the end of 2026-01 assumed growth of 16.7% on the same month a year earlier.
Units for 2026-03 to 2026-12 are projected at 218,192 over 10 months, at 661,413 USD of ad spend; 1 month of those stands on spend the app estimated.

The units model is fitted on 32 months, 2023-05 to 2026-02, and reads 0.2064 units per 1 USD of ad spend. Adding 2026-02 moved it from 0.2061 to 0.2064, a change of +0.0003 against a margin of 0.0437 either way (one standard error), which is inside that margin. It stands on what was entered in the forecasting app: 2 corrected units figures, 0 corrected ad spend figures, 1 month left out of training and 1 figure withheld. 1 correction sits on a source figure that has since moved.

The units model is fitted on 32 months, 2023-05 to 2026-02, and reads 0.2064 units per 1 USD of ad spend. limitations: Served from the copy the MixShift forecasting app published on 2026-09-30 (vintage 3). Corrections made in the app since then reach this answer on the app's next push, normally within a day.
2 of the months the units model trained on have corrected sales but uncorrected units; every units figure carries a blocking caveat saying so.
No brand plan is recorded yet: where a figure is compared with the year-start forecast, that forecast stands in for a plan and is not one.
